therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: CD38 targeting monoclonal antibody combined with PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: tumor cell targeting via CD38 and T-cell activation via PD-1 blockade
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: participants with lymphoma (classical Hodgkin lymphoma, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, peripheral T-cell lymphoma)
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: dose limiting toxicities and safety, with efficacy endpoints of complete response rate (cohort A1) and objective response rate (cohorts A2, B, C)

results.effect_size: ORR: cHL cohort A2 33.3% (95% CI: 12.3–60.9), DLBCL cohort B 5.9% (95% CI: 0.3–25.0), PTCL cohort C 9.1% (95% CI: 0.5–36.4); CR rate cHL cohort A1 27.8%
results.target_engagement_evidence: Isatuximab plasma concentrations achieved therapeutic levels with Cmax 181-265 mcg/mL and steady-state trough levels 122-390 mcg/mL. Cemiplimab achieved Cmax 70.9-90.8 mg/L with steady-state levels 60.6-139 mg/mL
subgroup_findings: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma showed better response rates than DLBCL or PTCL
safety_signals: Grade 3-4 lymphocyte count decreased common across cohorts
Grade 3-4 platelet count decreased in DLBCL and PTCL cohorts
Serious infections including pneumonia, sepsis, and viral infections
No dose limiting toxicities in cycle 1
results.dose_information: Isatuximab intravenous infusion, cemiplimab intravenous infusion, 28-day cycles

context.investigator_commentary: Trial was terminated. Limited efficacy observed except in classical Hodgkin lymphoma subgroup
